findings.title: Migration interpolates host directly into SQL
findings.body: File db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 25 builds INSERT with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) where h comes from the site_settings value. A host containing a single quote, backslash or SQL breaks out of the string literal and allows SQL injection / migration failure. Values from the database must be quoted with connection.quote or inserted via ActiveRecord, not string interpolation.

findings.title: Migration crashes when settings rows are missing
findings.body: File db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb lines 9-16 do execute(...)[0]['id'] and execute(...)[0]['value'] without checking for empty results. On a fresh database or where embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are absent, [0] is nil and calling ['id'] raises NoMethodError, failing the whole migration. It also calls .to_i on nil-derived values and uses cmd_tuples which is Postgres-specific.

findings.title: Update/destroy dereference nil when host not found
findings.body: File app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 10 and 15 do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy. If the id does not exist, host is nil, so save_host calls nil.host= and destroy calls nil.destroy, raising NoMethodError and returning 500 instead of 404. An attacker or stale admin UI can trigger it.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: File app/models/embeddable_host.rb lines 5-8 call self.host.sub! twice unconditionally. If host is nil (blank form submission, API call without host param), this raises NoMethodError: undefined method sub! for nil instead of failing validation cleanly. Guard for blank host before stripping scheme/path.

findings.title: Hosts with ports never match
findings.body: File app/models/embeddable_host.rb: before_validation keeps the port (only strips scheme and path) so example.com:8080 is stored with port, but record_for_host extracts URI#host which strips the port and queries lower(host) = ? with the bare hostname. A stored host with a port will therefore never be found by host_allowed?, breaking embedding on non-standard ports. Normalize consistently and downcase the lookup value for the case-insensitive query.

findings.title: Embedded _ids array handling crashes on null
findings.body: File app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 line 198 does obj[k].map(...) when the key ends in _ids. If the server returns null for that key (e.g. color_ids: null), calling map on null throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole record. Must guard for null/non-array before mapping.
